extracted.intended_audience: communication scholars, journalism and public relations researchers, advanced students, and professionals interested in media–PR relations
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing PR influence on news coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical content-analysis study of how parliamentary press releases affect newspaper coverage (Saxon state parliament, Feb–Jul 2000), using the intereffication model to assess mutual adaptation between PR and journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chance of a press release being noticed
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nur 28 Prozent der Pressemitteilungen hatten eine Chance, von mindestens einer Zeitung beachtet zu werden." / "Merely 28 percent of the releases had a chance to be noticed in at least one of the papers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical measure of visibility: proportion of all press releases that stood any chance of being picked up by newspapers. Used as an outcome metric for PR success; implies that the majority of releases receive no coverage opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of press releases to overall coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a fourth of the total coverage of parties in parliament was occasioned by their press releases. ("nur ein Viertel der Gesamtberichterstattung über die Fraktionen ging auf diese Pressemitteilungen zurück.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies the share of newspaper reporting that can be attributed to PR-originated material; a low share indicates limited direct influence of press releases on overall reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of journalist editing when press material is used
rubrics_metrics.description: When press releases were used, they were mostly heavily edited by journalists. ("Wenn Pressematerial verwendet wurde, dann meist unter starker Bearbeitung der Journalisten.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative/operational indicator: extent to which journalists alter PR texts before publication. Suggests that presence of PR material in coverage does not equal verbatim reproduction — evaluate by measuring editing intensity or substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between news value and extent of editorial reworking
rubrics_metrics.description: Press material was edited by journalists more the higher the news value and thus the alleged importance of the subject. ("und zwar umso mehr, je höher der Nachrichtenwert und damit die vermeintliche Bedeutung des Themas war.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies an interaction: high-news-value topics prompt stronger journalistic reworking of PR content. Use news value as a moderator when assessing how PR materials are transformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR controllable factors: frequency of releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Political PR can, in certain degrees, affect its own success, most strongly by the frequency with which it appears. ("Politische PR kann bedingt Einfluss auf ihren eigenen Erfolg nehmen, vor allem durch Frequenz...")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive implication for PR practitioners: increasing release frequency can raise chances of being noticed; frequency is a measurable strategy variable to evaluate PR effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR controllable factors: journalistic presentation/style
rubrics_metrics.description: Political PR can affect its success by using journalistic style. ("...und by using journalistic style." / "...und durch journalistische Aufbereitung.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that the format and style (e.g., journalistic framing, lead, inverted pyramid) of press materials influences uptake; evaluate press releases for adherence to journalistic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of newspaper editorial tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper’s editorial leanings noticeably interact with the chances for success of a party’s PR. ("Redaktionelle Tendenzen einer Zeitung interagieren jedoch spürbar mit den PR-Erfolgschancen einer Partei.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual moderator: newspaper ideology/line or editorial policy affects whether and how PR is used. When evaluating PR success, account for outlet-level editorial tendencies as covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intereffication model: mutual adaptation between PR and journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the intereffication model both the adaption of journalism to PR and, vice versa, of PR to journalism can be ascertained. ("Auf der Grundlage des Intereffikations-Modells ... sowohl Adaptionsleistungen des Journalismus an die PR wie auch umgekehrt der PR an den Journalismus ermitteln.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical heuristic for analyzing the PR–journalism relationship: treat influence as bidirectional and interactive rather than unidirectional determination. Use intereffication to frame hypotheses and interpret findings about adaptation and counter-adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological standard: independent and comparative coding
rubrics_metrics.description: The 486 press releases and 823 newspaper articles were coded both independently and comparatively. ("Die Basis bilden 486 Pressemitteilungen und 823 Zeitungsbeiträge ... die jeweils unabhängig voneinander sowie abgleichend codiert wurden.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research-methods criterion: perform independent coding of PR materials and news items plus comparative coding to assess links/adaptations. Implies use of reliability checks and cross-referencing to attribute coverage to press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization of PR success via measurable outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: PR success operationalized through measurable indicators such as noticeability rate (28%), share of coverage attributable to PR (25%), and qualitative measures of editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for evaluation design: combine quantitative counts (visibility rates, share of coverage) with qualitative content-change metrics to assess PR effectiveness comprehensively.
